paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage teaches: Jesus sees you before you ever see Him. He was alone on land that night, and He could see His disciples straining to row (Mark 6:48). Nobody had to flag Him down or send up a flare. If you're pulling hard against the wind right now, He sees that too.

Then look at what He says when they're terrified: "Take courage! It is I. Do not be afraid." (Mark 6:50). He doesn't hand them a lecture. He gives them Himself, and then He climbs in the boat with them. The wind dies down only after He's there (Mark 6:51), and that tells me the answer to a scary night is Jesus coming close, not a better rowing technique.

Now the part that makes me sit down on my gold base. Mark says the disciples had not understood about the loaves, and their hearts had been hardened (Mark 6:52). Keep that one in your pocket, friend, because it means a person can stand right next to Jesus and still miss who He is. Meanwhile the people at Gennesaret ran, begged, and reached for just the fringe of His cloak, and all who touched Him were healed (Mark 6:56). So the question for you is simple: what are you going to do with what Jesus has already shown you? Run to Him, like they did.
